compliance.status: binding resolution accepting DCA numbers (no objections filed)

notes: Borough Council adopted Resolution #25-41 (January 28, 2025) accepting DCA's Fourth Round Present Need of 0 and Prospective Need of 218. No objections filed. Court Order dated May 5, 2025 accepted obligations. Fourth Round VLA results in RDP=12 and Unmet Need=206. Prior/Third Round: combined 278-unit obligation (83 Prior Round + 195 Third Round) with RDP=30 and Unmet Need=248 per 2016 FSHC settlement. Fourth Round RDP mechanism: (1) Brookside/BCUW 100% affordable family/supportive at Block 1014/Lot 2.01 — 1 balance credit; (2) The Crossings inclusionary at 619 N Maple Ave (Block 1016/Lots 3,5,11) — 2 balance credits; (3) 111 First Street inclusionary at Block 1015/Lot 13.01 — 1 credit; (4) Life Opportunities group home at Ferris Court (Block 102/Lot 19) — 4 special-needs credits + 2 bonuses; (5) New municipally-sponsored unit — 1 proposed credit; + 3 bonuses = 12 RDP. Fourth Round Unmet Need (206): addressed via Downtown Inclusionary Overlay Zones (~23.5 acres, OL-1 to OL-4, 20% set-aside, potential 56 affordable units) + Borough-wide Mandatory Set-Aside Ordinance (20% for-sale / 15%→20% rental).

sources.title: Ho-Ho-Kus Borough Fourth Round Housing Element and Fair Share Plan (Adopted May 8, 2025)
sources.excerpt: Based on the updated 2025 Fourth Round VLA, the Borough has a Fourth Round RDP of 12... As a result of the Borough's Fourth Round VLA update, the Borough has a Fourth Round Unmet Need of 206 units... the Borough's Downtown Inclusionary Overlay Zones encompass a little less than 23.5 acres of the Borough's Downtown... Using an average density of 12 dwelling units per acre across the 23.5 acres of the Downtown Inclusionary Overlay Zones, there may be a total of 56 affordable housing units that would potentially be provided through redevelopment.

sites.developer: Bergen County United Way (BCUW) / Madeline Corporation
sites.quote: Brookside is a 100% affordable, 13-unit development producing 14 credits located on Brookside Avenue near the Ho-Ho-Kus rail station (Block 1014, Lot 2.01). The project was developed pursuant to the Third Round developer's agreement between the Borough and Bergen County United Way / Madeline Corporation Partnership ('BCUW / Madeline Partnership')... The project received a CO on May 1, 2023.
sites.notes: 13 of 14 credits applied to Prior/Third Round RDP. 1 remaining credit applied to Fourth Round RDP. 1 Fourth Round bonus credit (municipally funded 100% affordable site). Controls through at least 2051.

sites.site_name: The Crossings at Ho-Ho-Kus (619 N Maple Avenue)
sites.quote: The Crossings was initially approved as a 53-unit inclusionary mixed-use development located at 619 N Maple Avenue (Block 1016, Lots 3, 5, and 11) consisting of ground floor retail and 53 units with a 15% affordable set-aside of eight (8) family rental units. Subsequently, the Borough approved 10 additional total units of which two (2) would be affordable from a 20% set-aside.
sites.notes: 8 of 10 affordable credits applied to Prior/Third Round RDP. 2 remaining family rental credits applied to Fourth Round RDP. Controls through at least 2054.

sites.quote: Pursuant to the Chamberlain Settlement Agreement, Frasco Realty constructed an inclusionary development at 612-614 Maple Avenue (Block 1015, Lot 9). The project consists of three (3) market rate units, one (1) affordable family rental unit, and retail space on the ground floor. The project was issued a CO on February 22, 2021.
sites.notes: 1 credit applied to Prior/Third Round RDP per Chamberlain Settlement Agreement. Controls through at least 2050.

sites.quote: 111 First Street contains an inclusionary affordable rental unit located within the OL-1 inclusionary overlay zone on Block 1015, Lots 13.01 (formerly Lots 13-14). The site contains a total of eight (8) units, of which one (1) unit is an affordable three-bedroom unit that is reserved for a low-income household... A CO was issued on August 5, 2024. The affordable unit has minimum thirty-year affordability controls through at least 2054.
sites.notes: 1 credit applied to Fourth Round RDP (generates Fourth Round VLA RDP as built inclusionary development). Also generates development fee credit for fractional units.

sites.site_name: Life Opportunities Unlimited Group Home (Ferris Court)
sites.adoption_status: under renovation (as of April 2025; conversion to 4-bedroom group home)
sites.quote: Life Opportunities Unlimited, an experienced group home provider throughout Bergen County, owns and will operate a group home for adults with special needs in the Borough on Ferris Court (Block 102, Lot 19). The group home will contain four (4) very low-income bedrooms for individuals with special needs.
sites.notes: 4 special-needs credits toward Fourth Round RDP + 2 bonus credits (N.J.S.A. 52:27D-311.k(1) — special needs/permanent supportive housing).

sites.quote: The Borough will produce one (1) municipally-sponsored family affordable rental dwelling unit. The Borough anticipates that the affordable unit will be provided on Borough-owned property and/or religious/non-profit owned property.
sites.notes: 1 credit toward Fourth Round RDP. Low-income, 2- or 3-bedroom, 40-year affordability controls. Estimated cost up to $750,000. Specific location TBD.

sites.site_name: Downtown Inclusionary Overlay Zone (OL-1 through OL-4)
sites.current_zoning: R-2 Residential, R-4 Residential, GB General Business
sites.proposed_zoning: Downtown Inclusionary Overlay (OL-1 to OL-4, Ord. 2017-10; amended Ord. 2018-03)
sites.quote: The Borough adopted an inclusionary overlay zoning district (§85-13.1 of the Borough Code) on July 25, 2017, by Ord. No. 2017-10... The overlay zone encompasses approximately 23.5 acres of the Borough's Downtown... Using an average density of 12 dwelling units per acre across the 23.5 acres of the Downtown Inclusionary Overlay Zones, there may be a total of 56 affordable housing units that would potentially be provided through redevelopment at the required twenty percent (20%) affordable housing set-aside in the Downtown Zones.
sites.notes: Primary mechanism for addressing Fourth Round Unmet Need of 206 (plus cumulative Prior/Third Round Unmet Need of 248). Four overlay subdistricts: OL-1 through OL-4, densities 6-15 du/ac, 2-3 story max. 20% set-aside for GB zone (upper stories, ground floor non-residential) and R-2/R-4 zones. Flood hazard area; proximity to NJ Transit rail station.

sites.adoption_status: adopted (amended March 27, 2018; to be further amended for rental set-aside to 20%)
sites.quote: The Borough's Affordable Housing Ordinance (Chapter 2 of the Borough Code) establishes a Borough-wide mandatory set-aside that applies to any multi-family or single-family attached development created through any municipal rezoning, or a Zoning Board action, use or density variance, redevelopment plan, or rehabilitation plan that provide for densities at or above six (6) units per acre. The required set-aside of for-sale units is 20%, and the required set-aside for rental units is 15%. The Borough will amend the mandatory set-aside section of the Affordable Housing Ordinance to require a minimum set-aside of 20% for rental units.
sites.notes: Applies at ≥6 du/ac. 20% for-sale; 15% rental (to be amended to 20% rental). Does not supersede Downtown Inclusionary Overlay in the Downtown. Supplemental mechanism for addressing cumulative Unmet Need.
